subject: Physics
title: Distance vs Displacement
summary: Distance counts the whole path you walked; displacement only looks at the straight line from start to end, with its direction.
keyPoints: **Displacement** = straight line from start to end, with direction (vector).
|Displacement| ≤ distance (equal only for straight-line motion in one direction).
Back at the start: displacement = 0, distance ≠ 0.

blocks.alt: A walk 4 m east then 3 m north, with the 5 m displacement arrow
blocks.caption: Distance 7 m, displacement 5 m.

blocks.formula: For two perpendicular walks a and b:  displacement = √(a² + b²)

list: Home → school → home (1 km each way): distance 2 km; displacement 0.
Half a circle of radius r: distance πr; displacement 2r (the diameter).
One full lap of a circular track: distance 2πr; displacement 0.

quiz.q: A runner goes 6 m north then 8 m east. The displacement is:
Can displacement be greater than distance?
quiz.explain: The straight line is the shortest path, so |displacement| ≤ distance.

quiz.q: A car goes 5 km forward and 5 km back. Its displacement is:
quiz.explain: It ends where it started, so the displacement is 0.

quiz.q: For half a circle of radius r, the displacement is:
quiz.explain: Start and end are opposite ends of a diameter: 2r.

simulation.reason: Choosing different paths between the same points and watching distance grow while displacement stays fixed (or returns to zero) is exactly the comparison this topic is about; the existing Speed vs Velocity simulation already does it, so it is reused.
simulation.objective: Compare the path length with the straight start-to-finish arrow for different paths.
instructions: Pick a path: straight, there-and-back, zig-zag or circle.
Press Play or drag the time slider.
Compare the distance with the displacement readout.
On there-and-back and the full circle, watch the displacement return to zero.
